source_name: Open Contracting Partnership — OCDS Data Registry (search & bulk download)
why_relevant: Authoritative registry of which jurisdictions publish OCDS-structured procurement data, with API/bulk-download links. It is the fastest way to establish whether Montenegro (CeJN) has any machine-readable, standardised publication or whether ME data must be sourced from aggregators and scrapers instead.

source_name: Opentender.eu (DIGIWHIST / Government Transparency Institute)
why_relevant: EU-funded transparency scraper covering ~33-35 jurisdictions (TED + national portals) with red-flag indicators and downloadable datasets. Montenegro does NOT appear in its stated coverage (Serbia and North Macedonia do), so its main value here is (a) a regional benchmark for RS/MK against which ME can be compared, and (b) reusable open-source scraping/analytics code on GitHub.

source_name: Global Public Procurement Database (GPPD) — Montenegro country profile (World Bank)
why_relevant: World Bank-hosted cross-country procurement database with a dedicated Montenegro profile — a normalised, third-party aggregation of ME procurement indicators and (where available) transaction data, useful for baselining market size and buyer concentration without a commercial subscription.

source_name: opendata.gov.me — tender-tagged datasets (Montenegro open data portal)
why_relevant: State open-data portal exposing tender-tagged datasets (reportedly including open-procedure procurement registers with API access). Although state-run rather than commercial, in this cell it functions as the free structured alternative to paid aggregators and is the natural baseline for measuring aggregator added value.

source_name: MAPS e-procurement assessment of Montenegro's public procurement system (2024)
why_relevant: Independent 2024 assessment documenting how the CeJN e-procurement system publishes data, what is machine-readable, registration volumes and gaps. It is the authoritative reference for judging what any aggregator can actually harvest from ME and where aggregators must fill holes — essential input to the access-review of every paid platform in this cell.

source_name: DRI — Revizorski izvještaji archive (audit report repository, 2004–present)
why_relevant: The actual archive of final audit reports, filterable by year, audit type and audited entity. This is where regularity audits containing procurement findings live, going back roughly two decades — multi-year series no primary portal offers.

source_name: DRI — IT / information-system audits (revizija informacionih sistema)
why_relevant: DRI runs a dedicated IT-audit line (2 IT audits in a recent year alongside 25 regularity and 6 performance audits). These reports describe the procured systems, the vendors, IT security/continuity gaps and the contracting history — the closest thing in Montenegro to an independent assessment of state IT/payment-adjacent system procurement.

source_name: DRI — Godišnji izvještaj o izvršenim revizijama i aktivnostima (annual audit activity report)
why_relevant: Annual consolidated report giving the year's audit programme, systemic procurement findings and recommendation follow-up. Best single document for tracking which entities are under audit scrutiny and which procurement failure modes recur.

source_name: Institut alternativa — Aktuelno / news stream (paginated)
why_relevant: Deep-paginated archive (140+ pages observed) that surfaces IA's own analyses plus references to other actors, official reports and datasets. A good snowball spine for discovering procurement-monitoring publications and events over a decade.

source_name: mojnovac.me — IA budget transparency database (70,000+ budget items)
why_relevant: IA-built structured database of Montenegrin budget execution from 2011 onward, searchable by economic and organizational classification. Lets you size the spending envelope (e.g. IT/services lines) of a bank-adjacent public buyer even when the individual contract is unpublished — a derived-data source no primary portal offers.

source_name: mojgrad.me — IA local-government budget portal
why_relevant: Municipal budget data for all Montenegrin local governments, maintained by IA for years. Municipalities are significant buyers of POS/IT/payment services and their direct-award share (~17% per IA) is where portal coverage is weakest.

source_name: MANS — National Integrity System assessment (NIS, Transparency International methodology)
why_relevant: Institution-by-institution assessment of Montenegro's oversight bodies (anti-corruption agency, DRI, independent bodies, SOEs) using TI methodology. Gives a calibrated view of which oversight sources are actually credible and enforceable — useful metadata for weighting every other source in this cell.

source_name: Balkan Tender Watch (regional coalition incl. MANS) — Montenegro section
why_relevant: Regional CSO coalition (OSF Serbia/BiH/Kosovo, MANS for Montenegro, CCC North Macedonia) producing comparative procurement analyses and 'corruption-risk tender' quantifications across the Western Balkans — including findings that Montenegro leads on annulled procedures. Cross-country benchmarking that no single national source provides.

source_name: Agencija za sprječavanje korupcije (ASK) — antikorupcija.me
why_relevant: Montenegro's anti-corruption agency; publishes annual and quarterly work reports, integrity-plan oversight, conflict-of-interest and lobbying findings that touch procurement decision-makers. Its own procurement plan is also published, making it a template for how such plans are disclosed.

source_name: ASK on X/Twitter (@ASK_CrnaGora)
why_relevant: Low-latency announcement channel for ASK findings and report publication, useful as a trigger for pulling the underlying PDF rather than polling the site.

source_name: Centar za građansko obrazovanje (CGO/CCE) — procurement & anti-corruption research
why_relevant: NGO producing studies on municipal procurement practice ('Kako nabavljaju crnogorske opštine?'), corruption perception, and institutional integrity (PAKT project). Complements IA/MANS with a local-government and public-perception angle; hosts a large PDF library at media.cgo-cce.org.

source_name: Centar za istraživačko novinarstvo Crne Gore (CIN-CG) — Istraživanja
why_relevant: Investigative newsroom that reconstructs contracts and money flows from FOI and registry data, including work on money flowing under the 'information technology' activity code and on state spending via work contracts. Functions as a de-facto auditor of contracts that never surfaced officially; often co-publishes with Vijesti.

source_name: SIGMA/OECD — Montenegro monitoring reports & Western Balkans procurement overviews
why_relevant: External, methodologically consistent audit-like assessment of Montenegro's procurement system: legal/institutional set-up, remedies effectiveness, transparency, and the central procurement institutions. Multi-year series (2017, 2019, 2024) enabling trend analysis and cross-WB benchmarking that no national watchdog produces.

source_name: Open Government Partnership — Independent Reporting Mechanism (IRM) reports on Montenegro
why_relevant: Independent third-party evaluation of Montenegro's open-government commitments, historically including procurement transparency and proactive publication of contracts. Documents commitments made and not delivered — useful for explaining why certain contract data is missing from the portal.

source_name: gov.me FOI disclosure archive (informacije kojima je pristup odobren) — MANS/NGO requests
why_relevant: Government publishes documents released under freedom-of-information requests, many of them filed by MANS. This is where contracts and annexes that were never proactively published actually become public — an oversight-driven leak channel into otherwise-missing award data.

source_name: Parliament of Montenegro FOI archive (arhiva.skupstina.me) — approved-access documents
why_relevant: Legacy parliamentary archive of documents released to NGOs (MANS among them) under FOI, plus the parliamentary track where DRI audit reports are formally considered. Complements the executive-branch FOI archive with legislature-side records.

source_name: Dan (dan.co.me) — Montenegrin daily newspaper
why_relevant: Confirmed to run aggregate procurement accountability reporting with hard numbers — e.g. state institutions and enterprises spending EUR 309m on public procurement with EUR 19.5m spent outside tender procedures, broken down by goods/services/works. Opposition-leaning daily that names institutions and irregularities; a fast channel for procurement controversy.

source_name: Vijesti (vijesti.me) — leading independent Montenegrin daily
why_relevant: Montenegro's most-read independent daily and the outlet the cell brief names first for tender/award/controversy reporting. Not directly returned by my searches (search results skewed to portals and Wikipedia), so listed on cell-brief grounds with reduced confidence — its economy desk is the expected home of contract-award and cancelled-tender stories that never reach primary notice portals.
